endorsements.quote: Each tier demands tailored oversight, validation and governance, with increasing levels of statutory regulatory scrutiny (eg., European Union Artificial Intelligence Act and U.S. Food and Drug Administration) and clinical supervision.
Training in AI literacy and automation bias.
Audit logging with periodic quality review and feedback loops.
Governance actions include formal clinical validation and clearly defined intended-use boundaries.
Multidisciplinary approval with continuous monitoring and change-control for model updates with regulatory assessment where applicable.
If explored, restricting the use to ethics-approved prospective studies with explicit consent, real-time human override and independent safety monitoring.
As such, healthcare organisations must proactively develop clear, institution-specific protocols and ethical guidelines to bridge these regulatory gaps and ensure compliance.
Governance actions include mandatory clinician review and confirmation before outputs are used in care.

unlisted_practices: Require human sign-off for any externally shared LLM-generated content in low-risk applications.
Adopt local standard operating procedures and approved prompt templates for low-risk LLM applications.
Avoid routine deployment of critical-risk LLM applications that autonomously prescribe or diagnose without clinician oversight.
Explore AI-to-AI supervision using multiple independent AI models to cross-validate outputs.
Conduct prospective evaluations comparing LLM-assisted workflows versus usual care using predefined safety endpoints.

screen.reason: This is a commentary proposing a clinician-led, risk-stratified framework to guide the responsible adoption and governance of LLMs in healthcare.
